meta.title: Pinned allowlist of AWS Config managed rule IDs referenced by this framework
meta.purpose: The registry generator extracts backtick-quoted AWS Config managed rule identifiers from the guidance prose in traceability/aws-service-ksi-map.json. Prose is not a safe source of executable rule identities: a shorthand or an 'or X equivalents' aside can leak a token that is not a real AWS Config managed rule (e.g. 'aurora', which is not a managed rule - AWS has specific rules such as rds-cluster-multi-az-enabled). This allowlist pins the exact set of real managed-rule IDs the framework references. build_collector_registry.py rejects any extracted token that is not on this list, so a bogus identifier fails the build instead of becoming a config_managed_rule check target.
meta.source: Curated from the AWS Config managed-rules catalog; every id here is a real AWS Config managed rule. Add an id here ONLY after confirming it against the current AWS Config managed-rules documentation.
meta.catalog_identifiers: Each rule name paired with its AWS Config catalog identifier (the Source.SourceIdentifier a deployed managed rule carries), read from the per-rule page of the AWS Config Developer Guide. The identifier is NOT a transform of the name: four differ (restricted-ssh is INCOMING_SSH_DISABLED, restricted-common-ports is RESTRICTED_INCOMING_TRAFFIC, cloudtrail-enabled is CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED, multi-region-cloudtrail-enabled is MULTI_REGION_CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED). automation/importers/import_findings.py resolves a deployed rule by this identifier from a describe-config-rules export; the vocabulary test asserts the two lists stay aligned.
